title: Nonpositivity from bounded half-steps
statement: Let $s$ be a subset of a set $X$, and let $f:X\to\mathbb R$. If the image $f(s)$ is bounded above and, for every $x\in s$, there is a $y\in s$ such that $f(x)\le f(y)/2$, then $f(x)\le0$ for every $x\in s$.
hypotheses_covered: s is a subset of a type X
f maps X to the real numbers
the image f(s) is bounded above
for each x in s, there exists y in s with f(x) ≤ f(y)/2
replaced: Let $s$ be a subset of a set $X$ and $f:X\to\mathbb R$. If $f(s)$ is bounded above and every $x\in s$ admits $y\in s$ with $f(x)\le f(y)/2$, then $f(x)\le0$ for all $x\in s$.
